clusters.mechanism: RuntimeCatalog mutations (patch/delete/re-add) leave ProviderTracker.modelBlocks keyed by the unchanged catalog ID, so a stale rejection of the old backend blocks the replacement backend for up to 24 hours.
PATCH merge preserves the old effort when omitted and rejects null/default as invalid, so an existing runtime model's default effort cannot be cleared.
Provider probe results are recorded without a generation/ordering guard, so a late older probe overwrites a newer served-model discovery result.
Factory constructor throws on stored runtime models that collide with code/config models or reference a removed provider, so the daemon fails to boot and the API cannot be used to recover.
scripts/smoke.ts now opens the live production DB (running migrations) and silently drops checks for disabled or missing providers, beyond what was requested.
Route tests decode the :id path param themselves, so they never verify that the real router decodes the encoded slash (%2F) in model ids.
Pre-existing smoke.test.ts escaped-process fixtures are flaky or failing independent of this change.
Eval runner's availability check bypasses Router.route() and omits the tracker.notServed() guard, so unserved models can still be called.
probeProvider publishes provider status on every probe even when nothing changed, adding needless publishes and served_models queries.
The change exceeds the ~350 source-line budget.
